description_short: Bhante Bodhidhamma explores the Buddha's teaching on śūnya (voidness/emptiness) as another expression of anattā (not-self), drawing from the Mahā-suññata Sutta.
description_long:
In this comprehensive talk, Bhante Bodhidhamma examines the Mahā-suññata Sutta (Greater Discourse on Voidness), exploring how the Buddha taught liberation through understanding śūnya—the emptiness or insubstantiality of all phenomena. The discourse reveals how voidness (śūnya) is simply another way of expressing anattā (not-self), showing the Theravāda roots of concepts later developed in Mahāyāna Buddhism.

The Buddha emphasizes the importance of solitude and withdrawal from meaningless social engagement for serious practitioners, while teaching a systematic approach to recognizing the three characteristics of existence in the five khandhas (aggregates). Bhante explains how this contemplation of arising and passing away leads to the abandonment of the conceit 'I am' and ultimate liberation.

The talk also addresses the proper relationship between teachers and students, discussing how even advanced practitioners can fall away from the path through attachment to sensual pleasures. The Buddha's famous potter analogy illustrates how a true teacher continually guides students through repeated instruction and testing, helping them develop both liberation and purity of heart. This teaching offers practical guidance for contemporary practitioners on maintaining Right Awareness while engaging skillfully with worldly pleasures without attachment.
